report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of 5 of worktree.py, focusing on docstring/comment claims. All claims are either kept or uncheckable; no broken claims found in this chunk.

handoff.purpose: Define low-level filesystem helpers and the recursive tree removal function with extensive invariant documentation.

symbols.name: _clear_readonly
symbols.note: Best-effort removal of read-only bit on a path.

symbols.name: _unlink_reparse_point
symbols.note: Removes a reparse point (symlink/junction) without following it.

symbols.name: _force_unlink
symbols.note: Unlinks a file, retrying with read-only clearance on PermissionError.

symbols.name: _force_rmdir
symbols.note: Removes a directory, retrying with read-only clearance on PermissionError.

symbols.name: _chain_between
symbols.note: Returns path components from root to target, key-based comparison.

symbols.name: _remove_tree_no_follow
symbols.note: Recursively deletes root without traversing reparse points, with per-syscall verification.

symbols.name: _verify_reachable
symbols.note: Inner function of _remove_tree_no_follow; re-verifies that the path to target is safe.

claims.text: Drop the read-only bit git sets on loose objects, best effort.
claims.why: Function catches OSError and does nothing on failure.

claims.text: Remove the LINK itself. Never touches what it points at.
claims.why: Uses os.rmdir (for directory symlinks/junctions) and os.unlink (for file symlinks); does not follow links.

claims.text: A directory symlink / junction is removed with rmdir, a file symlink with unlink; which one applies differs by platform and link kind, so both are tried.
claims.why: The code tries os.rmdir first, then os.unlink.

claims.text: Walked upward by comparison KEY rather than with relative_to, which is case-sensitive and would raise on Windows for a differently-cased spelling.
Raises ValueError if root is not on target's path.
claims.why: Raises ValueError when parent == current (reached filesystem root without finding root).

claims.text: EVERY path handed to a syscall that RESOLVES it -- os.scandir, os.rmdir, os.unlink, os.chmod -- is re-classified with a FRESH lstat IMMEDIATELY beforehand, together with every component above it, up to and including guarded_ancestors.
claims.why: In the while loop, _verify_reachable is called before each action (scan, unlink, rmdir). The drain (os.rmdir) is not shown in this chunk but is mentioned as present in the full function.

claims.text: There are exactly three such sites (the scan, the per-child unlink, the rmdir drain) and all three verify.
claims.why: The drain (os.rmdir) is not in this chunk; the claim about its verification cannot be checked here.

claims.text: Raises OSError on failure and WorktreeRemovalRace if a reparse point appears above ANY step -- the scan, the unlinks, or the drain.
claims.why: _verify_reachable raises WorktreeRemovalRace if a reparse point is found; the function does not catch OSError, so it propagates.

claims.text: A partial delete is reported, never swallowed.
claims.why: The function does not catch exceptions from _verify_reachable or the removal operations; partial delete raises an exception.

claims.text: That sentence was false as written until 2026-07-28: the drain had no verification, so a partial delete THROUGH a swapped ancestor was neither detected nor reported, and cleanup_worktree returned normally on top of it.
claims.why: The drain is not in this chunk; cannot verify the claim about its current state.

claims.text: Does it exist at all? That is the only question answered here. Whether a path is a reparse point, a file, or a directory is decided in exactly ONE place -- when it is POPPED, immediately before it is opened -- and the root is not special-cased.
claims.why: The code calls os.lstat(root) only to check existence; classification happens in the while loop via _verify_reachable and _is_reparse_point.

claims.text: RE-VERIFIED PER CHILD, not once per directory.
claims.why: In the for loop over entries, _verify_reachable(child) is called for each child.

claims.text: A FRESH lstat, deliberately not entry.stat(): on Windows the DirEntry's stat is served from this scandir's cache (measured), so asking the DirEntry would re-introduce the stale read.
claims.why: The code calls os.lstat(current) on line 462 (not entry.stat()), and the comment explicitly says to avoid the cache.

claims.text: mutation testing shows the suite does NOT go red if it is deleted, and that is not an oversight in the tests -- it is redundant on this platform, measured both ways.
claims.why: This claim refers to test suite behavior not present in this chunk.

observations.what: The `_remove_tree_no_follow` function contains a long, detailed docstring that includes historical bug descriptions, performance measurements, and known limitations. This is unusual for a docstring and indicates the function has been carefully scrutinized.

The claim about three verification sites (scan, per-child unlink, rmdir drain) cannot be fully verified because the drain code is not in this chunk. The docstring states it is verified, but the code is absent.

The docstring mentions that the drain had no verification until 2026-07-28, but the current code (chunk) does not include the drain. This raises the question of whether the drain is now correctly verified.
The chunk ends mid-sentence in the comment about mutation testing. The full comment suggests that a branch is redundant but the code is kept for clarity. The conclusion of that thought is missing.
